claims.claim: Chipotle’s business model is a pure restaurant‑sales model – the company generates revenue solely from food and beverage sold at its owned and partner‑operated locations.
claims.quote: Our revenue is derived from sales by our restaurants.

claims.claim: The brand is positioned around a purpose‑driven narrative that emphasizes responsible sourcing and sustainability, which the company uses as a differentiator.
claims.quote: Chipotle is a brand with a demonstrated purpose of Cultivating a Better World.

claims.claim: Management frames growth as a five‑pillar “Recipe for Growth” that aims to improve competitive standing through operational and digital enhancements.
claims.quote: Our Recipe for Growth strategy leans into what uniquely differentiates Chipotle, with a focus on accelerating growth and sharpening competitiveness.

claims.claim: Management identifies AI‑driven technology and a refreshed loyalty program as key levers for future growth.
claims.quote: Modernize our business model with industry‑leading technology, including leveraging AI and relaunching our Rewards Program, to elevate the experience for our guests and teams;

claims.claim: Digital ordering accounted for more than one‑third of total food‑and‑beverage sales in 2025 and is a primary growth driver.
claims.quote: Digital sales represent food and beverage revenue for company‑owned restaurants generated through the Chipotle website, Chipotle app or third‑party delivery aggregators and include revenue deferrals associated with Chipotle Rewards. Digital sales represented 36.7% of food and beverage revenue in 2025, compared to 35.1% in 2024.

claims.claim: In Q3 2026, the share of digital sales rose further, indicating continued momentum in the digital channel.
claims.quote: Digital sales represented 38.8% of total food and beverage revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase from 36.7% for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

claims.claim: The company operates a predominantly owned‑store footprint in the U.S. with limited partnership expansions abroad.
claims.quote: We own 3,938 Chipotle restaurants throughout the United States… and 104 international Chipotle restaurants. Additionally, we had 14 international partner‑operated restaurants.

claims.claim: A material portion of revenue (≈ 16 %) depends on third‑party delivery platforms, exposing the business to channel risk.
claims.quote: Over 16% of our 2025 food and beverage revenue consisted of delivery orders for which we are reliant on third‑party delivery companies.

claims.claim: Competitive pressure comes from both traditional restaurant rivals and growing delivery‑aggregator platforms.
claims.quote: The fast‑casual, quick‑service, and casual dining segments of the restaurant industry are highly competitive … Competition from food delivery services, which offer meals from a wide variety of restaurants, also has increased in recent years and is expected to continue to increase.

claims.claim: Management views responsible‑sourcing as a differentiator but acknowledges that rivals make similar claims, potentially eroding that edge.
claims.quote: We believe our commitment to higher‑quality and responsibly sourced ingredients resonates with guests and gives us a competitive advantage; however, many of our competitors also make claims related to the quality of their ingredients … the use of these claims by competitors, even if such claims are not accurate or comparable, may lessen our differentiation.

claims.claim: Digital sales have risen year‑over‑year, underscoring its role as a strategic growth engine.
claims.quote: Our digital platform continues to be a strategic driver of our growth. Digital sales represented 36.7% of food and beverage revenue in 2025, compared to 35.1% in 2024.

claims.claim: Q3 2026 saw the addition of 84 new stores, with a majority (63%) featuring the Chipotlane drive‑through format, signaling a focus on convenience.
claims.quote: In the third quarter we opened 84 company‑owned restaurants, of which 53 included a Chipotlane, and five international partner‑operated restaurants.

claims.claim: The company plans to open roughly 350‑370 new locations in FY 2026, with a strong emphasis (≈ 80 %) on Chipotlane integration.
claims.quote: For 2026, management continues to anticipate the following: • Full year comparable restaurant sales growth in the low single digit range • 350 to 370 new restaurant openings, which includes 10 to 15 international partner‑operated restaurants. Around 80% of new company‑owned restaurants will have a Chipotlane.

claims.claim: Management expects operating cash flow to fund continued expansion without requiring external financing.
claims.quote: We believe that cash from operations, together with our cash and investment balances, will be sufficient to meet ongoing capital expenditures, working capital requirements and other cash needs for the foreseeable future.

claims.claim: Food‑safety risk remains a material concern despite extensive controls.
claims.quote: Food safety is our top priority, and we dedicate significant resources to ensuring that our food products are safe; however, even strong preventative controls and interventions from farm to restaurant cannot completely eliminate food safety risks.

claims.claim: Technology reliance creates exposure to cyber‑risk, especially given third‑party involvement.
claims.quote: We are heavily dependent on information technology systems … many of these critical systems are provided and managed by third parties, and we are reliant on these third‑party providers to implement protective measures that ensure the security and availability of these systems.

claims.claim: Supply‑chain capacity, particularly for responsibly sourced proteins, could constrain the pace of restaurant openings.
claims.quote: We have set aggressive goals for the number of new restaurants we plan to open over the next few years… We have experienced and may in the future experience limited available supplies of Responsibly Raised proteins and ingredients that meet our Food with Integrity specifications.

claims.claim: Year‑over‑year sales momentum slowed in 2025, and management projects roughly stagnant comparable sales in 2026.
claims.quote: Our comparable restaurant sales decreased 1.7% for the year ended December 31, 2025… For 2026, management is anticipating comparable restaurant sales to be about flat.

claims.claim: Full‑year 2025 revenue grew modestly, indicating underlying demand resilience.
claims.quote: Total revenue increased 5.4% to $11.9 billion.

claims.claim: Cost‑of‑goods‑sold pressure eased slightly YoY, partly due to menu price increases.
claims.quote: Food, beverage and packaging costs decreased 0.2% as a percentage of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

claims.claim: Labor expenses rose modestly YoY, reflecting wage inflation and lower sales volumes.
claims.quote: Labor costs increased 0.4% as a percentage of total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the year ended December 31, 2024.

claims.claim: Tax rate pressure increased in Q3 2026, driven by nondeductible expenses and reduced credits.
claims.quote: The effective income tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 25.6%, an increase from 23.1% in the third quarter of 2025.

gaps: The 10‑K does not provide quantitative forecasts for FY 2026 comparable restaurant sales growth beyond the forward‑looking statement in the cautionary note (no specific percent). The only numeric outlook appears in the earnings release (low‑single‑digit range).
Specific details on the cost impact of the new AI‑enabled technology rollout are mentioned as a strategic focus but no quantified cost or timing data are disclosed.
The 10‑K mentions sustainability targets (50% GHG reduction by 2030) but provides no interim 2026 progress metrics.
insight: Insight: Digital sales increased to 38.8% of total food and beverage revenue in Q3 2026, up from 36.7% in Q3 2025, highlighting accelerating adoption of Chipotle’s digital platform — EX‑99.1 line 29: "Digital sales represented 38.8% of total food and beverage revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase from 36.7% for the three months ended September 30, 2025."
